name: Cabin Crew
title: Air Hostess & Cabin Crew
intro: From Class 12 to flying as cabin crew: there is no national exam — each airline selects you, then trains you to DGCA safety requirements before line flying.

phases.title: Finish Class 12 and build the basics
phases.summary: Any stream works; spoken English and customer-service skills matter more than subjects.
points: Most airlines ask for a Class 12 pass from any stream; some prefer a degree or a hospitality diploma.
Fluent spoken English matters most; Hindi, a regional or a foreign language is an advantage, especially for international airlines.
Customer-service experience helps you in interviews.

phases.title: Check the airline rules and apply directly
phases.summary: Each airline publishes its own age, height, BMI and vision rules — read the notice before you apply.
points: Watch official airline career pages; each airline runs its own recruitment rounds.
Age, height, BMI and vision limits are set by each airline in its recruitment notice.
Private academies are optional: useful for grooming, English and interview practice, but their certificate is not a DGCA licence.
phases.tip: Genuine airlines never ask for money to give you a job. Apply only through the airline's official careers page and avoid agents who charge for "placement".

phases.title: Clear airline selection
phases.summary: Group discussion, interview, grooming check and medical.
points: Selection rounds usually include a group discussion, a personal interview and a grooming check.
Medical fitness is checked as DGCA requires for cabin crew, before training starts.
Men and women are both recruited — flight stewards and air hostesses do the same job.

phases.title: Initial cabin crew training
phases.summary: The airline trains you in safety, emergency, first-aid and service, to DGCA requirements.
points: Airlines train cabin crew to the safety training requirements set by DGCA before you fly on the line.
Training covers safety and emergency drills, first aid and in-flight service.
Type-specific training prepares you for the aircraft your airline flies.

phases.title: Line flying and growth
phases.summary: Supervised flights first, then full crew duties; recurrent checks keep you approved.
points: You start with supervised flights, then take on full crew duties.
Yearly safety refreshers and type-specific training keep you approved to fly; medical fitness is renewed through the career.
Growth path: cabin crew → senior crew → purser / cabin manager → trainer or in-flight service manager; after flying, airport services, airline training and hospitality roles.
facts: Fixed pay + flying allowance (varies by airline)
